To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

BFOA optimized FPI/FPIDs controller outperforms PSO, FA, BFOA, and hybrid BFOA-PSO-based PI controllers for traditional power system, PSO and ABC-based PI controllers for reheat system and GA and hybrid FA–based PSO-based PI controller for hydrothermal system.
a BFOA-optimization technique for FPI/FPIDs is developed for AGC of a two-area restructured power system with hydrothermal sources.

BFOA optimized fuzzy PI/PID controllers have better dynamic performance and superior robustness than PSO, FA, BFOA and hybrid BFOA-PSO based PI and fuzzy PI controller based upon pattern search and particle swarm optimization algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of BFOA optimized FPI/FPIDs for AGC of traditional/restructured MSMA power systems.
the design of FPI/FPIDs for AGC of MSMA power systems.
the development of a novel BFOA-based FPI/FPD controller for AGC, which can handle the uncertainties and non-linearities of the multi-area power system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FPI/FPD controller optimized by BFOA is an effective controller for AGC in traditional and restructured power system.
the proposed FPI/FPD controller is a superior alternative for AGC of traditional/restructured power systems.
the BFOA-based FPI/FPAD controller is able to perform satisfactorily for the traditional as well as restructured power systems under study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed BFOA-based FPI/FPD controller is able to handle both traditional and restructured power systems with improved performance in comparison with PS, PSO, FA and hybrid FA– PSO-based PI controllers.
the proposed BFOA- optimized FPI/FPIDs controller is capable of performing automatic generation control of both traditional and restructured power systems in an efficient manner.
the proposed controller is able to handle the uncertainties of the systems under study, which makes the controller robust for practical implementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed FPI/FPIDs controller can effectively handle both traditional and restructured power systems and can also be implemented on other power system structures.
the BFOA is a powerful tool in the optimization of fuzzy PI/PID controllers for automatic generation control.
the proposed BFOA-based fuzzy PI/PID control scheme is able to achieve a good compromise among the transient and steady-state performance of the AGC system.
